Australia | industry = Educational Travel, Holidays | services = [[Holiday camp]]s and activities | owner = Midlothian Capital Partners | website = {{Official URL}} }} '''PGL Travel Ltd''' is a provider of school activity courses and [[summer camp]]s for children in the United Kingdom.{{Cite web|url=http://www.independent.co.uk/news/obituaries/peter-gordon-lawrence-550381.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220524/http://www.independent.co.uk/news/obituaries/peter-gordon-lawrence-550381.html |archive-date=2022-05-24 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live|title=Peter Gordon Lawrence|date=August 31, 2004|website=The Independent}} Along with [[NST (company)|NST]], European Study Tours and StudyLink it is a part of the HB Education group, owned by [[Midlothian Capital Partners]]. == History == PGL was established in 1957 by Peter Gordon Lawrence as PGL Voyages. In the 1960s and early 1970s, its market was young adults and based on three main activities – canoeing, sailing and pony trekking – with accommodation in tents. PGL moved into the school and group travel market and expanded in the 1980s, purchasing more properties, ranging from a mansion house in [[Perthshire]] to a converted farm in [[Oxfordshire]]. PGL opened a headquarters in the South of France and became one of the first UK organisers of canoeing holidays in the [[Ardèche (river)|Ardèche Gorge]]. [[File:Canoes at Drummond's Dub - geograph.org.uk - 899890.jpg|thumb|left|Canoes at Drummond's Dub centre, Herefordshire]] In the early 1990s, the acquisition by the company of the former Quest Outdoor Adventure programme, and of a number of centres operated by competitors, resulted in a considerable expansion in the schools' adventure market in the UK and France. In 1993, the company entered the school ski market with the acquisitions of Ski Europe and Ski Wessex. [[File:Lésigny Château de Grande Romaine 1.jpg|thumb|Château de Grande Romaine, France]] In 2000, PGL purchased Château de Grande Romaine, a 300-bed former hotel and grounds on the eastern outskirts of Paris. In July 2004, PGL agreed to buy its biggest rival, 3D Education and Adventure from [[Center Parcs UK and Ireland|Center Parcs]] for £12 million, in order to allow Center Parcs to focus on improving its holiday villages,{{Cite web |date=2011-07-29 |title=3D Education & Adventure (part of Center Parcs) {{!}} Oxygen Consulting |url=https://oxygen-consulting.co.uk/3d-education-adventure-part-of-center-parcs/ |access-date=2024-12-30 |website=Oxygen Consulting {{!}} Compelling strategic insight for organisations connected to the global health & fitness industry |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=22 July 2004 |title=Center Parcs sells 3D business to focus on holiday villages |url=https://www.healthclubmanagement.co.uk/health-club-management-news/Center-Parcs-sells-3D-business-to-focus-on-holiday-villages/8534 |website=Health Club Management}} which added three more centres to PGL's portfolio on the South Coast of England, one on the Isle of Wight, and a contract with [[Pontins]] to provide children's activities at their holiday parks under the name 'Go Active', which ended in 2010 when Pontins entered administration.{{Cite news |last1=Finch |first1=Julia |last2=Treanor |first2=Jill |date=2010-11-13 |title=Pontin's falls into administration as fond memories fail to save firm |url=https://www.theguardian.com/business/2010/nov/13/pontins-administration-holiday-camps |access-date=2025-03-03 |work=[[The Guardian]] |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}} [[File:PGL holiday group enjoying zip wire - geograph.org.uk - 5369090.jpg|thumb|left|Zipwire, [[Sedlescombe]]]] In December 2005, PGL suspended three staff members following allegations of inappropriate behaviour involving alcohol, guns and drugs. The allegations were substantiated by photographs showing the staff members engaging in misconduct at their former centre in South Wales. The Children's Commissioner for Wales and the [[NSPCC]] condemned the actions, with Natalie Cronin of the NSPCC stating, "they exposed children to unnecessary danger. This behaviour could have resulted in a child suffering serious harm".{{Cite web |title= |url=https://www.pressreader.com/uk/daily-mail/20051212/281913063519220?srsltid=AfmBOopC5G8gkm6EO7bHsMd5zVXKZCR0vs1ekxxL3_pOHmmWUpY1OI4d |access-date=2024-12-30 |via=[[PressReader]]}} In response to the incident, PGL bosses admitted they were "shocked and embarrassed" and initiated an internal investigation, implemented stricter policies and enhanced staff training to prevent such incidents in the future.{{Cite news |date=2005-12-12 |title=Staff suspended at adventure camp |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/wales/mid_/4521504.stm |access-date=2024-12-30 |website=[[BBC News Online|BBC News]] |language=en-GB}} The company was sold in 2007 to [[Holidaybreak]] plc{{Cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/business/2007/may/18/8|title=Multimillion pound windfall for PGL bosses|first=Simon|last=Bowers|newspaper=[[The Guardian]] |date=May 18, 2007|via=www.theguardian.com}} and formed the first part of that company's Education Division. Property acquisitions in the UK included [[Caythorpe Court]], near Grantham, in 2004{{CN|date=February 2025}} and in 2009, [[King Edward's Place]] near Swindon in Wiltshire, which trades as PGL Liddington.{{Cite news |date=2010-05-13 |title=Adventure centre creates 106 jobs |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/wiltshire/8679930.stm |access-date=2026-05-08 |work=BBC News: Wiltshire |language=en-GB}} [[File:The lake, Boreatton Park - geograph.org.uk - 65372.jpg|thumb|Water events, Boreatton Park, [[Shropshire]]]] In July 2011, Holidaybreak was purchased by [[Cox & Kings]] Limited, based in India. In 2014, PGL opened an office in [[Melbourne]], Australia, and acquired two centres in Victoria and one in Queensland: Campaspe Downs, Camp Rumbug and Kindilan. [[File:Newby Wiske Hall (geograph 5642713).jpg|thumb|[[Newby Wiske Hall]], [[North Yorkshire]]]] In 2017, PGL sought to acquire two new centres: [[Newby Wiske Hall]] (formerly North Yorkshire Police Headquarters){{cite web |date=2017-03-16 |title=North Yorkshire Police announce sale of headquarters of 40 years near Northallerton |url=http://www.itv.com/news/calendar/2017-03-16/north-yorkshire-police-announce-sale-of-headquarters-of-40-years-near-northallerton/ |access-date=2018-04-27 |publisher=[[Itv.com]]}} and [[Bawdsey Manor]] on the Suffolk Heritage Coast.{{cite web |author=Megan Goodwin |date=24 March 2017 |title=Bawdsey Manor purchased by adventure holiday company PGL |work=[[East Anglian Daily Times]] |url=http://www.eadt.co.uk/news/bawdsey-manor-purchased-by-adventure-holiday-company-pgl-1-4947422 |access-date=2018-04-27 }} PGL's largest area of business continues to be school trips and educational travel. These range from activity and adventure trips to subject focussed trips such as science, ICT, Maths, Field Studies and French Language courses. During the UK school terms, PGL mainly offers school and youth group holidays, as well as birthday parties and day trips. Outside of term times, PGL also offers family and child-only adventure holidays (summer camps).{{Cite web |title=PGL |url=https://www.girlguiding.org.uk/about-us/our-partners-and-supporters/pgl/ |access-date=2022-03-30 |website=[[Girlguiding]] |language=en}} In 2020, the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom|coronavirus pandemic]] had an effect on its business, leading to disputes with customers concerning refunds.{{cite news | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-52565927 | title=Hard-up parents plea for refunds from PGL travel firm | work=[[BBC News Online|BBC News]] | date=6 May 2020 }} In October 2021, [[Ofsted]] suspended the registrations of four PGL-operated activity centres in England due to serious safeguarding concerns. These issues included environmental health and safety violations, as well as allegations of staff misconduct involving substance misuse.{{Cite news |last=Badshah |first=Nadeem |date=2021-10-28 |title=Four activity centres in England suspended over 'serious' safeguarding concerns |url=https://www.theguardian.com/education/2021/oct/28/four-activity-centres-in-england-suspended-over-serious-safeguarding-concerns |access-date=2025-03-03 |work=[[The Guardian]] |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}{{Cite web |date=2021-10-29 |title=Ofsted suspends kids holiday centre activities over safeguarding issues |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-wiltshire-59088298 |access-date=2025-03-03 |website=[[BBC News Online|BBC News]] |language=en-gb}} In June 2023, at Guildford Magistrates Court, the company pleaded guilty to violations of Section 33 of the [[Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974]]. Subsequently, on 2 October 2023, at Staines Magistrates Court, they received a £1 million fine, £18,006 in costs, and a £181 victim surcharge. The court learned that since 2009, PGL had been aware of 520 children across its sites who had suffered finger injuries from doors, some severe enough to cause amputation, yet failed to proactively install finger guards to prevent future incidents.{{Cite web |title=£1 million fine for outdoor education provider in Waverley |url=https://www.waverley.gov.uk/Council-updates/Read-our-latest-news/1631-million-fine-for-outdoor-education-provider-in-waverley |access-date=2024-12-30 |website=[[Borough of Waverley|Waverley Borough Council]] |language=en-GB}} In January 2025, PGL acquired three new centres: [[Grosvenor Hall (estate)|Grosvenor Hall]] in [[Ashford, Kent|Ashford]]; [[Dearne Valley]] in [[Doncaster]] and [[Overstrand Hall]] in [[Cromer]] from Inspiring Learning Group, who operated Kingswood activity centres,{{Cite web |last=McDowell |first=Tim |date=2025-01-17 |title=PGL Beyond announces package of support following Inspiring Learning Group entering Administration |url=https://pglbeyond.com/pgl-beyond-announces-package-of-support-following-inspiring-learning-group-entering-administration/ |access-date=2025-07-01 |website=PGL Beyond |language=en-GB}} one of PGL's biggest rivals in a rescue deal, to ensure that the planned residential trips for over 50,000 young people that year could go ahead. The acquired centres would trade under the PGL name until the end of the season when they would undergo a full transition. PGL also announced they would accept new bookings from impacted Kingswood customers at the price previously agreed with Kingswood, and further reduce that price to recognise any monies previously paid.{{Cite web |date=2025-01-18 |title=Outdoor learning company closes seven UK activity centres |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c3w81pdnw18o |access-date=2025-07-01 |website=[[BBC News Online|BBC News]] |language=en-gb}} == Abroad == PGL has centres in France for school groups and other youth groups - which offer both activity and educational holidays - and 3 centres in Australia for school groups, youth and other groups, and school holiday camps. === France === * Château de Grande Romaine, [[Île-de-France]] * Domaine de Segries, [[Ardèche]] === Australia === * PGL Camp Rumbug (South Gippsland, Victoria) * PGL Campaspe Downs (Kyneton, Victoria) * PGL Kindilan (Redland Bay, Queensland) == References == {{reflist|30em}} == Sources == *[https://www.independent.co.uk/news/business/sharewatch/the-investment-column-vantis-in-demand-as-companies-feel-the-strain-875791.html The Independent], 24 July 2008 *[https://www.ft.com/content/110dbd2a-c97b-11e0-9eb8-00144feabdc0 Article from The FT on acquisition by Cox & Kings], 18 August 2011 *[http://www.travelweekly.co.uk/articles/37772/holidaybreak-accepts-312m-cox-kings-takeover-bid Article from Travel Weekly], 27 July 2011 *[http://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/services/travel/cox-kings-subsidiary-pgl-expands-footprint-in-australia/articleshow/28962833.cms Article on expansion to the Australian market], 17 January 2014 *[https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/wiltshire/8679930.stm BBC article on purchase of PGL Liddington], 13 May 2010 == External links == *{{Official website}} *[https://www.pgladventurecamps.com.au/ PGL Australia website] {{Tourism in the United Kingdom}} [[Category:Travel and holiday companies of the United Kingdom]]
extract: PGL Travel Ltd is a provider of school activity courses and summer camps for children in the United Kingdom.  Along with NST, European Study Tours and StudyLink it is a part of the HB Education group, owned by Midlothian Capital Partners.
